nodes.label: PrintCAD Organic microservice (photo to neural mesh, port 8001)
nodes.rationale: Lives in its own uv project because its stack (PyTorch cu128, transformers) is heavy and incompatible with the main backend. Returns raw STL; the main backend repairs, scales and beds the mesh. Random seed per request, so resending the same photo yields variants.

nodes.label: TRELLIS engine (image-large, default)
nodes.rationale: Default because quality is far superior; costs ~6 GB resident VRAM and ~1-2 min per piece on an RTX 5060 Ti. Vendored at pinned commit 442aa1e with the flexicubes submodule.

nodes.label: TripoSR engine (legacy, faster but less detailed)
nodes.rationale: Kept as fallback via ORGANIC_ENGINE=triposr, pinned at commit 107cefd; faster and lighter (~1.4 GB weights) but much less detailed.

nodes.label: Windows no-CUDA-compile shims (xformers, kaolin, torchmcubes, open3d stub)
nodes.rationale: TRELLIS officially requires flash-attn/xformers, kaolin, nvdiffrast. By using only the mesh output (no texturing/render) native deps shrink to spconv-cu126 (prebuilt wheel, PTX JIT for sm_120). Local shims: xformers reimplemented over torch native SDPA, kaolin reduced to check_tensor, torchmcubes replaced by scikit-image marching cubes, open3d stubbed in memory.

nodes.label: Single-reconstruction lock (VRAM shared with Ollama)
nodes.rationale: One reconstruction at a time because the 16 GB VRAM is shared with Ollama; TRELLIS + qwen3-vl loaded together can OOM, in which case the user should unload the Ollama model first. Mesh is decimated to <=500k faces with fast-simplification before export.
